scope: Registered territory Journey routes, their Team counterparts, default Standard runtime projections, Classic source index, and starter Team recipes. Local imports, company editions and standalone optional games are not aggregated into core-mode totals.
countingPolicy: Default, supplemental and historical route counts overlap. Never sum route editions, difficulties, artwork variants or the Classic index into a unique-level total. Raw route rows are source inventory only.

defaults.validationScope: Standard compiler resolution; no command-route or human playtest claim

levels.name: First return
levels.routeDecision: Cross to the far rail or turn back to the near rail?
levels.lesson: Reaching reclaimed ground secures a live line; empty regions fill.

levels.name: Choose your share
levels.routeDecision: Take the nearby narrow slice now, or travel along the rail for a larger enclosure?
levels.lesson: A hit on an unfinished line sends visible impacts along it. Reach reclaimed ground before the craft-bound front arrives.

levels.name: Two keepers
levels.routeDecision: Separate the two keepers first or wait until they share one side?
levels.lesson: Two occupied regions can keep their field even though the closing line is reclaimed.

levels.name: Nearby shore
levels.routeDecision: Take the short exposed line to the near woven landing, or cross the open gap to establish the larger far landing first?
levels.lesson: Separate foundation islands offer different return values; neither is earned coverage and neither fills territory by itself.

levels.name: Island outpost
levels.routeDecision: Close the short western join from the home panel, or make the longer bent return to the offset eastern stitches before choosing the next enclosure?
levels.lesson: A broad home panel and two broken joining points create different return distances without adding a rule beyond foundations and keeper reads.

levels.name: Stepping stones
levels.routeDecision: Use the near seed landing to build a short spikelet chain, or bypass it for the broader central sun landing before choosing an upper or lower return?
levels.lesson: Five disconnected landings turn the early foundation lesson into a real route fork without adding a new rule.

levels.name: Two bays
levels.routeDecision: Work from the upper offset into the tighter western bay, or descend through the centre and use the lower offset against the wider eastern bay?
levels.lesson: A stepped divider still retains two occupied bays, but its unequal edges make departure height and capture order matter.

levels.name: Courtyard return
levels.routeDecision: Take the short outer bridge first, or move along the ring to choose an inward enclosure?
levels.lesson: The ring separates two keeper-held fields. Its outer edge offers short returns; its inner edge supports larger enclosures. Both fields matter to the clear.

levels.name: Long way home
levels.routeDecision: Join through the upper shoulder group for the shorter first return, or descend to the offset gathered group for a longer line that approaches the far shoulder?
levels.lesson: Offset paired groups around a strong side-to-side joining axis make route planning visible while retaining only known foundation rules.

levels.name: Behind the patrol
levels.routeDecision: Slip behind the perimeter patrol onto the broad crossbar, or wait longer and descend the open stair to its safer inner tip?
levels.lesson: An asymmetric interior return can trade immediate access for a safer later departure while the outer patrol keeps its established route.

levels.name: Second landing
levels.routeDecision: Close the short near aperture after the perimeter patrol passes, or leave its open side and make the longer outside wrap to the offset far window?
levels.lesson: An open square and separated landing change return distance while keeping the known foundation, keeper and perimeter-patrol rules.

levels.name: Long rail
levels.routeDecision: Use the central stem for a short ordinary closure, or commit to a separated outer branch that improves the later return toward an optional bonus window?
levels.lesson: A stem and two offset branches create route value without changing movement, patrol speed or the optional nature of bonuses.

levels.name: New frontier
levels.routeDecision: Close the short near shoulder for a modest contour change, or cross the open centre and close the far shoulder first for a larger frontier reroute?
levels.lesson: Two shoulders make the moving frontier consequence visible: a closure changes the boundary it follows, not its collision rule.

levels.name: Turn the corner
levels.routeDecision: Extend the short arm to redirect contour pressure, or reach around the long arm for more ground?
levels.lesson: Practice changing a frontier route before combining it with an outer patrol.

levels.name: Return pocket
levels.routeDecision: Leave the pocket through the upper woven band for a short keeper read, or stage on the lower band before sweeping toward the freeze bonus?
levels.lesson: Alternating foundation bands and negative-space mouths redirect travel without introducing a rule ahead of its taught campaign arc.

levels.name: Soft crossing
levels.routeDecision: Cross the short slow band into the upper openwork return, or travel around its clear eastern edge before committing to the lower offset return?
levels.lesson: Slow ground changes route cost, while two unequal returns make the safer detour useful rather than merely longer.

levels.name: Dry spine
levels.routeDecision: Use the upper shoulder to work around the western slow bed, or descend the spine and establish the lower shoulder beside the eastern bed first?
levels.lesson: An asymmetric spine changes which slow-field edge is the practical return without changing terrain physics.

levels.name: Wide approach
levels.routeDecision: Build from the west hook along the slow-field edge, or cross the wider ordinary approach and establish the eastern hook first?
levels.lesson: Linked but separated returns reward planning around the slow field while the frontier patrol keeps the changing boundary relevant.

levels.name: Cool the crossing
levels.routeDecision: Establish the near framed panel before enclosing the lethal bed, or cross the safe northern shoulder and build a longer approach toward the far panel?
levels.lesson: Three unequal returns frame the lethal field without turning it into a wall; neutralizing it still requires a valid enemy-seeded enclosure.

levels.name: Garden refuges
levels.routeDecision: Neutralize the nearer row from the spine, or loop around the ends to reach the far refuge first?
levels.lesson: Clear lanes between lethal rows are still unclaimed field, not guaranteed return ground.

levels.name: Neutral ground
levels.routeDecision: Cross the western slow bed directly from the side branch, or climb the safe stem and arc above the eastern hot bed for a faster but longer enclosure?
levels.lesson: The non-crossing branches supply safe staging while the existing slow and lethal beds retain their exact rules and cells.

levels.name: Folded corner
levels.routeDecision: Close beside the short inner fold, or follow the alternating bands to establish the longer outer shoulder before the frontier arrives?
levels.lesson: A stepped return can offer several landing lengths while the same moving-frontier rules remain predictable.

levels.name: Inside out
levels.routeDecision: Close the broad western mouth near the inner keeper, or cross the upper end field and work from the smaller eastern mouth against the outer keeper?
levels.lesson: Offset openings keep the inner and outer fields connected until a deliberate closure; the visible frame alone never decides retention.

levels.name: Four quarters
levels.routeDecision: Start with a small near quadrant, or use the spacious cross to tackle the larger region while its keeper is distant?
levels.lesson: Each occupied chamber retains its own field. Permanent cross lanes provide returns but do not earn coverage.

levels.name: Side-door bays
levels.routeDecision: Secure the nearby interrupted rim and its broad landing, or cross the open centre to reach the far reversed rim before its patrol returns?
levels.lesson: Unequal contour mouths create different timing windows even though every bay follows the same retained-region and frontier rules.

levels.name: Dogleg return
levels.routeDecision: Connect the short upper point of the central hook, or pass the broken offset bands to establish the east landing before the perimeter patrol arrives?
levels.lesson: Alternating woven-band-inspired walls obstruct movement but never close a cut. Slow thread remains field until enclosed and never acts as a return.

levels.name: Staggered circuit
levels.routeDecision: Use the short central pad and cross the slow woven field, or follow a clear staggered lane to the right rail before reshaping the frontier?
levels.lesson: Hutsul-woven-lane-inspired bands are blocking walls with visible open ends. Foundations close cuts; marked field slows only the exposed craft.

levels.name: Wake the yard
levels.routeDecision: Close the short central cutwork window and wake its roamer, or pass the offset square openings to establish the east window first?
levels.lesson: Reshetylivka-cutwork-inspired openings are formed from walls and empty field. Only reclaimed foundations close a cut, and waking a roamer changes the value of the central return.

levels.name: Split berths
levels.routeDecision: Connect the near sleeper’s corridor now, or establish a side return before joining the far berths?
levels.lesson: Only reclaimed ground supports an active roamer. An unclaimed gap can keep two return networks separate.

levels.name: Stepped return
levels.routeDecision: Return to the short upper step or the long lower arm while the warned roamer patrols the stepped foundation?
levels.lesson: A return closes the trail but does not protect the craft from an active roamer approaching along reclaimed ground.

levels.name: Between the rows
levels.routeDecision: Take the short west contour panel, or cross the clear upper field to reach the east panel before its frontier patrol returns?
levels.lesson: Kosiv-ceramic-inspired contour frames remain gameplay abstractions: walls block, slow washes affect exposed craft, and the middle foundation supports reclaimed-ground pressure.

levels.name: Broken yard
levels.routeDecision: Build an outside escape to the near platform, or neutralize the marked pocket before joining the far platform?
levels.lesson: An escape corridor needs a usable departure, not merely a connection to reclaimed cells occupied by a roamer.

levels.name: Sorting yard
levels.routeDecision: Take a broad outer slice, use a stub return around its baffle, or switch chambers before a roamer meets your landing?
levels.lesson: The two roamer lanes warn from the start. Each field chamber has two retaining keepers, so separating occupied pockets may bank only the trail.

levels.name: First fracture
levels.routeDecision: Use the short central lattice before its earned approach can erode, or cross the offset openings to bank the detached east reserve first?
levels.lesson: An Örnek-informed geometric grouping remains an abstract route lattice: foundations survive erosion, walls block movement and earned connections can reopen.

levels.name: Island reserve
levels.routeDecision: Join the near island through the slowing approach, or open the wider clear side and retain a second return?
levels.lesson: Isolated foundations provide dependable landings even when the earned links between them are vulnerable.

levels.name: Two districts
levels.routeDecision: Establish the shorter west relief panel before its eroder marks the approach, or cross the open upper field to reach the taller east panel first?
levels.lesson: Borshchiv-informed dense and open bands become unequal abstract route panels. Each district keeps its own eroder and field anchor; the permanent spine switches pressure, not ownership.

levels.name: Bank the crossing
levels.routeDecision: Capture the crossing anchor before expanding farther, or use the lower permanent lane to approach from the opposite side?
levels.lesson: A captured required objective protects its cell and one deterministic reclaimed path to a permanent foundation or outer rail.

levels.name: Five landings
levels.routeDecision: Bank the western connection first, or secure the eastern anchor while keeping a cross-shaped landing between both eroders?
levels.lesson: Two captured anchors can protect different connections; five foundations are return choices, not five mandatory chores.

levels.name: Staggered reserve
levels.routeDecision: Secure the slowing northern connection first, or enclose the southern danger pocket before banking its anchor?
levels.lesson: Capture order should make the next route easier, not demand that every repeated cluster be cleared.

levels.name: A return in reserve
levels.routeDecision: Take the short central band as soon as pursuit commits, or cross the open upper edge and bank the lower reserve before returning through the alternating bands?
levels.lesson: A Krolevets-informed band rhythm stays an abstract return network: the pursuer commits visibly, foundations close cuts and walls only screen movement and sensing.

levels.name: Two ways home
levels.routeDecision: Commit to the nearer west braid before the frontier reaches its shoulder, or feint through the centre and close at the east braid after the pursuer locks the old heading?
levels.lesson: Hutsul diagonal alternation becomes two original stepped return networks. Their offsets create different approach timings without changing pursuit rules.

levels.name: Dogleg transfer
levels.routeDecision: Use the short central dogleg to screen and close the first commitment, or cross the top edge to bank the outer compartment before working back through the lower hazard?
levels.lesson: Kosmach pysanka compartmental organization inspires an abstract layered board. Foundations close cuts and block sensing; nearby walls screen but never become return ground.

levels.name: Crossed bands
levels.routeDecision: Keep the obvious crossing after the interceptor locks your heading, or turn toward the central return and neutralize a different hazardous band?
levels.lesson: The interceptor warns and predicts only the observed heading. Its committed target does not follow a later turn.

levels.name: Pressure ladder
levels.routeDecision: Climb through short staggered returns and turn after each lock, or expose one longer route while the frontier patrol controls the next rung?
levels.lesson: Successive changes of heading beat prediction, but each landing also changes the frontier patrol route.

levels.name: Signal channels
levels.routeDecision: Feint toward the northern clear channel, or turn south after the lock while preserving room for the reclaimed-ground roamer?
levels.lesson: Interception pressures the current heading while capture can wake a different movement-domain threat; solve the two roles with different routes.

levels.name: Read the lock
levels.routeDecision: Close at the compact central landing during the first row warning, or chain that safe close directly into the lower corridor for a stronger second departure?
levels.lesson: A Kyiv-area woven-belt record informs only the long narrow cadence. The row lock remains telegraphed, foundations close cuts and band walls never become return ground.

levels.name: Cross the afterglow
levels.routeDecision: Connect the west landing through the open aisle, or establish the northern return before working around the baffle ends?
levels.lesson: A locked column threatens the exposed trail. A west landing and a northern landing offer different returns; baffles are walls, never return surfaces.

levels.name: Switchyard
levels.routeDecision: Join the shorter west stepped band before the frontier turns, or cross the row lock and neutralize the east hot pocket while establishing its longer return?
levels.lesson: A Polissia woven-curtain record informs only separated-band organization. Staggered foundations are returns; adjacent woven-band walls are obstructions, not substitutes.

levels.name: Split junction
levels.routeDecision: Connect the west hooked branch before the column lock reaches it, or establish the longer east branch and attack a dangerous corner from its floating end?
levels.lesson: A museum gerdan record informs only paired branching cadence. The two branches stay independent return networks and their wall accents remain blocking geometry.

levels.name: Crossbar depot
levels.routeDecision: Complete a north-south spine or an east-west link first when both a row and a column can lock?
levels.lesson: Two known emitters mark a cross. The permanent landing is a refuge from the lanes, not a switch that disables them.

levels.name: Cooling loop
levels.routeDecision: Use an earned shortcut across a cooled bank or connect permanent landings before erosion can reopen that route?
levels.lesson: Lanes and erosion use separate warnings. Foundations never erode; reclaimed hazards can reactivate if earned territory reopens.

levels.name: First link
levels.routeDecision: Capture the visible relay on the direct central line, or enter through the west band and make a longer side close before committing to the bridge?
levels.lesson: A Podillia woven-towel record informs grouped-square and terminal-band organization only. The numbered relay opens the matching connector; surrounding band walls never become return ground.

levels.name: Second approach
levels.routeDecision: Open the near west connector from its short landing, or escape to the perimeter and approach the far east relay from above before the frontier reaches that return?
levels.lesson: A museum kilim record informs bilateral balance and alternating-band cadence only. Each mirrored trigger owns one connector; visual symmetry never implies shared activation.

levels.name: Three compounds
levels.routeDecision: Open the short upper relay to gain a direct north return, or branch east through the longer exposed approach and secure the roamer-side connector first?
levels.lesson: A museum kilim record informs alternating branch direction and right-angle border rhythm only. Relay order changes the return network while every field keeper stays in its own domain.

levels.name: Spiral stores
levels.routeDecision: Break the western inward route at the top or the eastern route at the bottom before moving across the central spine?
levels.lesson: A shortcut changes return distance, not the meaning of the surrounding open field. Broad exits remain available before either relay.

levels.name: Nested relays
levels.routeDecision: Open the cross-ring link before taking the inner trigger, or use the open lower approach and preserve the shorter return for later?
levels.lesson: The field keeper, not a closed gate, retains each chamber. Numbered links change player routes without moving that keeper into another region.

levels.name: Watchpost exchange
levels.routeDecision: Use the first opened junction to move through the hub or work around the outside to reach the opposite relay before the frontier approaches?
levels.lesson: Each occupied chamber remains a separate field problem. A junction opens traversal, not an automatic chamber clear.

levels.name: Read the arrows
levels.routeDecision: Use the short marked centre run before the eastern keeper crosses it, or travel west on the perimeter and take the slower chevron-side landing for a quieter first return?
levels.lesson: A museum towel record informs central-diamond, staggered-triangle and outward-branch organization only. Walls block movement; arrows change speed only in unclaimed field and never force a turn.

levels.name: Survey markers
levels.routeDecision: Connect a distant side platform with the arrows or make the shorter northward return before crossing the open lower field?
levels.lesson: An interrupted line of landing platforms is not one continuous return. Check the next reclaimed segment before leaving.

levels.name: Windbreak weave
levels.routeDecision: Take the short marked north thread, or cross west through the alternating band openings to reshape the frontier before approaching another return?
levels.lesson: A museum woven-towel record informs alternating band width and checker-like offset only. Broken bands are walls with visible openings; only foundations and captured territory close cuts.

levels.name: Compass array
levels.routeDecision: Use the short central neck against the lower arrows or take the longer lateral approach with them?
levels.lesson: Shortest distance and shortest exposure need not be the same. Across an arrow is ordinary speed, not a sideways push.

levels.name: Outer loop
levels.routeDecision: Cross the shorter inner posts, including an against-arrow gap, or reposition along the long reclaimed U before taking the outer approach?
levels.lesson: A return loop supports movement but may become roamer territory. Marked speed never makes reclaimed ground universally safe.

levels.name: Long wave
levels.routeDecision: Ride the central down-arrow to the joined landing before a keeper contests it, or reposition west and close on the upper riser while preserving the centre for an emitter recovery window?
levels.lesson: A museum gerdan record informs parallel-strip and central-join organization only. Directional zones change craft travel time; the lane emitter keeps its own warning, commitment and recovery schedule.

levels.name: First relay
levels.routeDecision: Close quickly on the central ridge and accept both patrol domains for the shield approach, or travel west on the perimeter and bank the upper side landing before entering the chamber?
levels.lesson: A museum chest record informs tripartite and divided-ridge organization only. Carved-looking baffles are walls; only foundations and reclaimed territory close a cut.

levels.name: Twin receivers
levels.routeDecision: Secure the upper gallery approach first, or the lower landing, before turning around a receiver baffle?
levels.lesson: Deep receiver galleries share the Sentinel field. Choose returns outside the baffles before committing to an inner cut.

levels.name: Relay perimeter
levels.routeDecision: Take the immediate left-zone return, or cross the perimeter to the narrow central opening and establish the focused middle landing before choosing a shield order?
levels.lesson: A museum runner record informs five-zone, central-focus and mirrored-outer organization only. The existing relay opens permanent connectors; the surrounding bands remain blocking walls.

levels.name: Crown audience
levels.routeDecision: Reach the broad north return through the central opening, or establish the west side return first and work around the paired shield baffles from the outside?
levels.lesson: A museum carved-shelf record informs centre-with-paired-sides symmetry only. The four shield sites stay independent objectives and the boss release rule remains unchanged.

levels.name: Crossing complete
levels.routeDecision: Close quickly at the central upper focus before the frontier turns, or travel west on the perimeter and make the longer close beside the lethal belt for a quieter next departure?
levels.lesson: A museum towel record informs three-focus and nested-centre organization only. The stepped forms are walls; they do not close a cut.

levels.name: Final broadcast
levels.routeDecision: Open the upper protected link first, or invest in the lower anchor while the keeper and eroder occupy different corridors?
levels.lesson: A territory repair and a trail-impact closure race are familiar but different decisions. Permanent foundations, opened connectors and captured objective anchors protect the planned return.

levels.name: Returning light
levels.routeDecision: Take the exposed long centre crossing before the lane warning, or climb the home rail and bank the upper stepping return before waking reclaimed-ground pressure?
levels.lesson: A Krolevets towel record informs triangular side cadence and scattered-centre organization only. The small baffles mark route rhythm without becoming return ground.

levels.name: Home signal
levels.routeDecision: Use the short central dock close and accept immediate frontier pressure, or descend from home to establish the south wing before choosing the four-relay order?
levels.lesson: A museum tile record informs centre-to-four-points organization only. The finale still uses the familiar capture, relay and reclaimed-ground rules.

levels.name: Islands in concert
levels.routeDecision: Secure the upper petal from the central spiral shoulder, or connect the western dot first and build an outside return before separating the three keepers?
levels.lesson: Five familiar landings form an open spiral, petal and dot rhythm; the finale adds no mandatory mechanic.

levels.name: Living border
levels.routeDecision: Secure the central stem before the mixed patrols converge, or use a longer exposed crossing to establish the far offset leaf first?
levels.lesson: Offset returns make capture order matter while the known perimeter and moving-frontier patrol rules stay unchanged.

levels.name: Winding channels
levels.routeDecision: Secure the upper branch through slow ground, or descend the central stem and contest the lower branch beside the lethal channel first?
levels.lesson: A branched return network combines known terrain and patrol domains without adding a finale-only rule.

levels.name: Three open circuits
levels.routeDecision: Close the short western mouth under near-frontier pressure, or span the exposed upper field to establish the far circuit first?
levels.lesson: Three layered-resist-inspired circuits keep walls, foundations and hazardous field visually separate while known capture rules combine.

levels.name: Open frequency
levels.routeDecision: Connect the short central branch and release pressure onto it, or take the long upper route to the far outer cluster before joining either sleeper?
levels.lesson: A Petrykivka-informed branching composition combines known roles only: clustered returns, retained field, hazardous gaps, frontier pressure and two reclaimed-ground roamers.

levels.name: Keep the network
levels.routeDecision: Connect the short central open panel and accept roamer pressure, or take the long upper route to bank the remote outer panel before repairing the hub?
levels.lesson: A Krychevsky-informed open-panel composition combines known repair, anchor, frontier and reclaimed-ground threats without adding another rule.

levels.name: Close the circuit
levels.routeDecision: Keep disconnected fallback landings or connect a circuit that gives both the craft and frontier patrol new routes?
levels.lesson: Combine known impact, frontier and reclaimed-ground rules. This optional Remix adds no mandatory mechanic.

levels.name: Windows in the wire
levels.routeDecision: Spend the rest window linking another refuge, or close a smaller cut and preserve a corridor before the roamer wakes?
levels.lesson: Combine known lane, impact and reclaimed-ground threats. Moving enemies and an active lane both send visible fronts; direct craft contact remains immediate.

levels.name: Switchback exchange
levels.routeDecision: Spend the next attack window opening a new escape connection or enclose a smaller region while keeping the roamer dormant?
levels.lesson: Combine established relay, lane and impact rules. Opening a link changes return choices, not enemy attack periods.

levels.name: Return currents
levels.routeDecision: Secure the permanent return first or invest in an earned sideways shortcut that erosion may reopen into an arrow field?
levels.lesson: Combine known arrow, erosion and relay rules: foundations and opened connectors are permanent; earned marked territory can reactivate.

levels.name: Rings of return
levels.routeDecision: Open the release dock first, or use the marked northern approach to rearrange the frontier before disabling the other shields?
levels.lesson: Known arrows and permanent relays alter route efficiency, not the Sentinel cadence. No new rule is introduced in this optional Remix.

levels.name: Dawn circuit
levels.routeDecision: Complete the protected outer circuit through relay corners, or use the shorter marked center while field threats remain on opposite sides?
levels.lesson: This optional combination uses only known roles. The protected circuit and earned spokes have different erosion consequences; neither changes the capture contract.

levels.name: Cross-stitch crossings
levels.routeDecision: Close at the nearby diamond landing after a pursuit warning, or continue through the stepped opening toward the farther return?
levels.lesson: The pursuer locks one visible point on the live stitch-like trail; the wall motif blocks sensing but never closes the cut.

levels.name: Rushnyk bands
levels.routeDecision: Cross through the nearer alternating band before pursuit commits, or circle the end while preserving an inner strip as the fallback return?
levels.lesson: Alternating rushnyk-inspired openings change which side offers cover; pursuit and the outer patrol pressure different parts of the route.

levels.name: Pysanka sections
levels.routeDecision: Leave the spindle through the near oval opening, or use the segmented wall as a sight screen before reaching the far return?
levels.lesson: The open pysanka-inspired sections provide sight screens, not secret capture chambers; only real landings close the cut.

levels.name: Dnipro crossings
levels.routeDecision: Link the central landing to pass the staggered breakwater, or take the wider outer crossing?
levels.lesson: Shore platforms are real returns; staggered breakwaters and keepers in separated approaches make crossing order matter.

levels.name: Four motor landings
levels.routeDecision: Keep the direct motor-pad heading after the target locks, or turn toward an adjacent pad and leave the committed intercept behind?
levels.lesson: Interception predicts only the observed heading. The four motor-like pads provide deliberate alternatives after the visible lock.

levels.name: Circuit lanes
levels.routeDecision: Take the obvious straight trace, or provoke a lock and switch to the offset aisle through a broad work pad?
levels.lesson: Component-like walls make the alternate heading useful counterplay; the committed target never follows a later turn.

levels.name: Twin lens chambers
levels.routeDecision: Shape the bridge frontier before provoking interception, or feint into one open lens and turn toward the opposite landing after lock?
levels.lesson: The frontier patrol follows the changing boundary while the interceptor follows only a previously locked heading target.

levels.name: Toolbench weave
levels.routeDecision: Reclaim the middle aisle now and wake its roamer, or join an outer work mat first to preserve another escape?
levels.lesson: Opening the board can activate a new threat on reclaimed ground; the warning gives time to leave.

levels.name: Twin landings
levels.routeDecision: Connect the islands together, or establish opposite return routes first?
levels.lesson: Both craft build a shared route network from separate foundations. Specialist Support is available as an optional safety tool; no pulse is required to clear this mission.

levels.name: Stepping exchange
levels.routeDecision: Secure the nearer offset step first, or expose a longer line to the central bank so the opposite pilot gains the stronger next departure?
levels.lesson: Alternating-band organization informs the obstacle rhythm only. The stepped marks are walls; only reclaimed islands and completed cuts are returns.

levels.name: Divided workshop
levels.routeDecision: Work the mirrored outer chambers independently, or contest the open central zone first so either specialist can cross over and support the partner?
levels.lesson: Zoned runner organization informs the mirrored baffles and central focus only. The gaps remain deliberate passages; walls never become closure surfaces.

levels.name: Switchback partners
levels.routeDecision: Bank the outer pockets first, or approach the shared middle platform from opposite wall tips?
levels.lesson: One specialist establishes the winding approach while the other protects the crossing that turns the middle platform into shared ground.

levels.name: Shared detour
levels.routeDecision: Neutralize the slow west passage for a controlled centre approach, or close around the lethal east passage first and give the partner the faster shared route?
levels.lesson: Unequal openwork spacing informs the staggered passages only. Capturing a material bed neutralizes it; touching a wall still cannot finish a cut.

levels.name: Crossed gardens
levels.routeDecision: Neutralize an outer garden for the safer transfer, or expose a longer cut to the nested central bank so both specialists gain the stronger next launch?
levels.lesson: Nested and cross-band organization informs the route rhythm only. Walls block movement, while only foundations and completed cuts close a trail.

levels.name: Split orchards
levels.routeDecision: Take the plain offset band toward the middle, or enclose one orchard first so the partner can route around the still-dangerous opposite side?
levels.lesson: Alternating band density informs the mirrored baffles only. Captured material becomes ordinary ground, but the bent wall ends remain blockers.

levels.name: Weaver crossing
levels.routeDecision: Link a thin separator to the middle opening, or neutralize a broad material lane before the partner exchanges sides?
levels.lesson: Variable-width band organization informs the thread spacing only. The elongated opening is a route decision, not a copied textile motif.

levels.name: Shared lookout
levels.routeDecision: Take the short outside return and wake its roamer, or connect toward the middle landing before opening that escape?
levels.lesson: The Interceptor protects the longer exposed connection while the Disruptor controls the keeper window. A return earned by either craft becomes shared ground for both.

levels.name: Twin depots
levels.routeDecision: Wake the outer return patrols for quick perimeter access, or wrap the inner baffles to establish receiver landings first?
levels.lesson: Interceptor Support removes nearby travelling impacts while Disruptor Support slows nearby enemies. Rescue remains available to both players.

levels.name: Changing courtyard
levels.routeDecision: Neutralize the upper hazard before linking the courtyard, or establish the lower slow-field approach while the partner prepares a different exit?
levels.lesson: Removing a terrain hazard does not make every reclaimed route free of enemies.

levels.name: Last rendezvous
levels.routeDecision: Reach opposite stepping islands first, or connect along one flank and let a partner reopen the other approach?
levels.lesson: Combine known return networks, material decisions and wake-up timing without learning another rule.
